turns.patient_opening: Hi. I’m a 24-year-old man, and today I came in because I’ve had sharp pain with painful mouth ulcers or sores. I also have red skin lesions, and one of the lesions is bigger than 1 cm. The pain is around 2/10, and the pain feels like it’s pretty localized (about 7/10), and it started fairly quickly.

turns.doctor_question: Do you have any swelling in one or more areas of your body (for example, in your face, hands, legs, or around a joint)?
turns.patient_answer: No, I don’t have swelling anywhere. My rash/lesions are red, but there’s no swelling and no itching.

turns.doctor_question: Do you currently have a fever—either that you feel (hot/flushed) or that you’ve measured with a thermometer?
turns.patient_answer: I don’t think I have a fever. I haven’t measured my temperature, but I don’t feel hot or flushed.

turns.doctor_question: Do your skin lesions peel off or shed (for example, flaking or coming off in layers)?
turns.patient_answer: No, they don’t peel or shed. They’re just red lesions.

turns.doctor_question: When you feel the pain, does it feel **heavy** (like a dull, weighty pressure)?
turns.patient_answer: No, it doesn’t feel heavy or like pressure. It’s more sharp pain.

turns.doctor_question: Is the affected area located on the **right labia majora** (the outer fold of skin on the right side of your vulva)?
turns.patient_answer: I don’t have that area—so no, it’s not on the right labia majora.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel so tired that you’re unable to do your usual activities, or are you stuck in bed all day long?
turns.patient_answer: No, I’m not that tired. I can still do my usual activities.
